المعدة:
 جهاز التنفس الصناعى
 Pirelli group

sections.text: مقدمـة

هذا المستند يوضح خطوات الفحص 
الشهرى لجهاز التنفس الصناعى كما هو موضح عاليه.

هذا 
الجهاز هو جهاز تنفس الغرض منه حماية كاملة للتنفس فى جو ملوث بغازات سامة او فى 
حالة نقص النسبة الحجمية للاكسجين فى الجو المحيط عن 
17 % حيث يقوم الجهاز بعزل 
الشخص المستخدم تماما عن الجو المحيط به حتى فى اقصى درجات التلوث خطورة على 
الحياة.

وفترة استخدام الجهاز 
تكون حوالى نصف ساعة تزيد او تقل حسب الحالة الصحية للمستخدم ودرجة نشاطة ومجهودة 
العضلى وحالتة النفسية والعصبية وحالات الخوف التى تؤثر على سرعة التنفس ومن الممكن 
ان تقل فترة الاستخدام وتصل الى ربع ساعة فقط.

والجهاز مزود بجهاز 
تحذير صوتى يعمل تلقائيا عند فتح محبس الاسطوانه ثم يتوقف عند الاستخدام.

واذا بدأ الانذار يعمل 
اثناء الاستخدام فان ذلك يكون بمثابة تحذير بانه لابد من الخروج من منطقة التلوث 
الى منطقة الهواء النقى حيث يكون متبقى دقائق قليلة وتنفذ كمية الهواء بالاسطوانة.

والجهاز به صمام تخفيض 
الضغط يعمل على تخفيض ضغط الهواء الذاهب الى بلف التنفس الى 7 بار.

ويكون صمام التنفس فى 
حالة التشغيل العادى على وضع الضغط الموجب ويظهر ذلك بعلامة اللون الابيض على مبين 
الصمام

عندما يتنفس مستخدم 
الجهاز فان ذلك بسبب انخفاض الضغط الموجب الطبيعى لبلف التنفس وذلك يحرك ديفرام 
البلف الذى يدفع عامود التحكم لبلف عدم الراجع فينفتح مسار الهواء فينساب الهواء من 
صمام مخفض الضغط الى قناع الوجه اما عند عملية الزفير فان الديفرام يعود الى وضعة 
الاصلى ويقوم عامود التحكم لبلف عدم الراجع بغلق مسار الهواء مرة اخرى فيخرج هواء 
الزفير الى الجو عن طريق بلفى الزفير فى قناع الوجه

ومع استمرار الاستخدام 
ينخفض ضغط الاسطوانة حتى يصل مؤشر عداد الضغط الى نطاق اللون الاحمر فيقوم جهاز 
الانذار السمعى باصدار صوت تحذيرى للمستخدم بان كمية الهواء على وشك النفاذ.

فى حالة تلف او عد 
فاعلية صمام النفس الاوتوماتيكى يتم التحويل الى وضع التشغيل الاحتياطى ويظهر ذلك 
بعلامة اللون الاحمر على مبين الصمام وهو يقوم بالامداد بتيار هواء مستمر ويتم ضبطة 
على كمية الهواء المطلوبة للتنفس حيث ان الضغط فى الاسطوانة يقل بسرعة نتيجة تيار 
الهواء المستمر وفى هذه الحالة يجب الخروج بسرعة من منطقة التلوث

تم اعداد هذا المستند 
بواسطة المهندس / يسرى عبد الحليم عبد اللطيف واختبره المهندس / وصفى وليم ناشد كبير 
مهندسى ادارة السلامة والصحة المهنية 
وراجعه السيد المهندس 
/سليمان زكى سليمان مدير عام ضمان وتأكيد الجودة الفنية

افتح 
 بلف الاسطوانة فتصدر صفارة قصيرة من جهاز التحذير الصوتى كدليل على خروج 
 الهواء لانبوبة التنفس

وضع بلف التنفس على وضع التشغيل العادى (مبين صمام التنفس يكون

حمل

ارتداء 
 قناع الوجه وربطه جيدا لمنع التهريبات

بعد 
 ارتداء القناع يتم التنفس مرتين على الاقل للتأكد من سلامة عمل 
 صمام التنفس

بعد 
 تنفيذ ما سبق يكون المستخدم جاهز لبدء تنفيذ المهمة اخذا فى 
 اعتبارة ان يتوقف فورا عن اداء المهمة وترك المنطقة الملوثة فى 
 الحال اذا سمع الانذار الصوتى لجهاز التحذير من نفاذ كمية هواء 
 التنفس او اذا اشتم رائحة التلوث او شعر بصعوبة فى التنفس او 
 بوجود خطر مفاجئ

على 
 المستخدم ان يتأكد من قيمة الضغط كل فنرة على عداد قياس الضغط 
 الموجود على المنظم

sections.text: بعد الاستخدام

rows:
تصريف الضغط من خرطوم الضغط 
 العالى عن طريق التنفس حتى اخراج الهواء

لا يتم فتح صامولة الربط عند بلف 
 الاسطوانة عندما يكون عداد المنظم ما يزال يقرأ ضغط بل يجب تصريف الضغط اولا

يتم فحص الجهاز بعد الاستخدام 
 للتأكد من عدم وجود شروخات او اجزاء مكسورة او مفقودة فى كل من قناع الوجه 
 وانبوبة التنفس ومنظم الضغط وجهاز التحذير الصوتى وبلف التنفس

 بمواد سامة وذلمك لجعل الجهاز صالح لاعادة استخدامه ويتم اتباع

 بالمحلول اشطف بالماء النقى ثم

sections_en.text: Egyptian Electricity Holding Company
Maintenance Procedures Information System

rows: Equipment: Pirelli Group industrial breathing apparatus
Issued to: Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station

sections_en.text: Introduction
This document sets out the steps for the monthly inspection of the industrial breathing apparatus as shown above.

This apparatus is a breathing apparatus whose purpose is to provide complete respiratory protection in an atmosphere contaminated with toxic gases, or where the volumetric oxygen content of the surrounding air falls below 17%, as the apparatus isolates the user completely from the surrounding atmosphere even under the most life-threatening degrees of contamination.

The period of use of the apparatus is about half an hour, more or less depending on the user's state of health, level of activity and muscular effort, and psychological and nervous state, and on states of fear that affect the breathing rate; the period of use may fall to only a quarter of an hour.
The apparatus is fitted with an audible warning device that operates automatically when the cylinder valve is opened and then stops during use.

If the alarm starts to operate during use, this is a warning that the user must leave the contaminated area for an area of fresh air, as only a few minutes remain before the air in the cylinder runs out.
The apparatus has a pressure-reducing valve that reduces the pressure of the air going to the breathing valve to 7 bar.
The breathing valve is in its normal operating state on the positive-pressure setting, shown by the white mark on the valve indicator.

When the user of the apparatus breathes in, the natural positive pressure of the breathing valve falls, which moves the valve diaphragm; this pushes the control stem of the non-return valve, the air path opens and air flows from the pressure-reducing valve to the facemask. On exhalation, the diaphragm returns to its original position and the control stem of the non-return valve closes the air path again, so the exhaled air leaves to the atmosphere through the two exhalation valves in the facemask.

With continued use the cylinder pressure falls until the pressure gauge pointer reaches the red zone, at which point the audible alarm device sounds a warning to the user that the air supply is about to run out.

If the automatic breathing valve is damaged or ineffective, it is switched to the standby operating mode, shown by the red mark on the valve indicator; this supplies a continuous air flow, adjusted to the quantity of air required for breathing, since the pressure in the cylinder falls rapidly as a result of the continuous air flow. In this case the user must leave the contaminated area quickly.

This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed, Senior Engineer of the Occupational Safety and Health Department, reviewed by Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Technical Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan, Head of Damietta Power Station Sector. It was reviewed by the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Chemist Ahmed Abdullah.
Procedure to be Carried Out

rows: Open the cylinder valve; a short whistle sounds from the audible warning device as evidence that air is going out to the breathing tube
Set the breathing valve to the normal operating mode (the breathing valve indicator is on the white sector)
Carry the apparatus on the back, fix it and fasten the shoulder and waist straps
Wear the facemask and fasten it well to prevent leaks
After wearing the mask, breathe at least twice to make sure the breathing valve is working properly

After carrying out the above, the user is ready to start the task, bearing in mind that he must stop the task immediately and leave the contaminated area at once if he hears the audible alarm warning that the breathing air supply is running out, or if he smells the contamination, feels difficulty breathing, or senses a sudden danger
The user must check the pressure value from time to time on the pressure gauge on the regulator

sections_en.text: After Use

rows: Vent the pressure from the high-pressure hose by breathing until the air is expelled
Do not open the coupling nut at the cylinder valve while the regulator gauge is still reading pressure; the pressure must be vented first
Inspect the apparatus after use to make sure there are no cracks or broken or missing parts in the facemask, breathing tube, pressure regulator, audible warning device and breathing valve

sections_en.text: Apparatus Components

rows: Facemask fitted with a speech device

sections_en.text: Cleaning the Apparatus After Use
A cleaning operation is carried out after use, especially if the atmosphere is contaminated with toxic substances, to make the apparatus fit for reuse, as follows:

rows: Avoid using cleaning solutions that damage the rubber or plastic parts (such as alcohol)
The cleaning solution must be warm, provided its temperature does not exceed 45 °C
A soft brush may be used for this purpose
Clean all parts of the breathing apparatus thoroughly, especially the breathing tube and the facemask
After finishing cleaning with the solution, rinse with pure water and then dry with a stream of air

When the user of the apparatus breathes in, the natural positive pressure of the breathing valve falls, which moves the valve diaphragm; this pushes the control stem of the non-return valve, the air path opens and air flows from the pressure-reducing valve to the facemask. On exhalation, the diaphragm returns to its original position and the control stem of the non-return valve closes the air path again, so the exhaled air leaves to the atmosphere through the two exhalation valves in the facemask.
With continued use the cylinder pressure falls until the pressure gauge pointer reaches the red zone, at which point the audible alarm device sounds a warning to the user that the air supply is about to run out.
If the automatic breathing valve is damaged or ineffective, it is switched to the standby operating mode, shown by the red mark on the valve indicator; this supplies a continuous air flow, adjusted to the quantity of air required for breathing, since the pressure in the cylinder falls rapidly as a result of the continuous air flow. In this case the user must leave the contaminated area quickly.

Procedure to be Carried Out
Open the cylinder valve; a short whistle sounds from the audible warning device as evidence that air is going out to the breathing tube | 1
Set the breathing valve to the normal operating mode (the breathing valve indicator is on the white sector) | 2
Carry the apparatus on the back, fix it and fasten the shoulder and waist straps | 3
Wear the facemask and fasten it well to prevent leaks | 4
After wearing the mask, breathe at least twice to make sure the breathing valve is working properly | 5
After carrying out the above, the user is ready to start the task, bearing in mind that he must stop the task immediately and leave the contaminated area at once if he hears the audible alarm warning that the breathing air supply is running out, or if he smells the contamination, feels difficulty breathing, or senses a sudden danger | 6
The user must check the pressure value from time to time on the pressure gauge on the regulator | 7
After Use
Close the cylinder valve | 1
Vent the pressure from the high-pressure hose by breathing until the air is expelled | 2
Do not open the coupling nut at the cylinder valve while the regulator gauge is still reading pressure; the pressure must be vented first | 3
Inspect the apparatus after use to make sure there are no cracks or broken or missing parts in the facemask, breathing tube, pressure regulator, audible warning device and breathing valve | 4

Cleaning the Apparatus After Use
A cleaning operation is carried out after use, especially if the atmosphere is contaminated with toxic substances, to make the apparatus fit for reuse, as follows:
Avoid using cleaning solutions that damage the rubber or plastic parts (such as alcohol) | 1
The cleaning solution must be warm, provided its temperature does not exceed 45 °C | 2
A soft brush may be used for this purpose | 3
Clean all parts of the breathing apparatus thoroughly, especially the breathing tube and the facemask | 4
After finishing cleaning with the solution, rinse with pure water and then dry with a stream of air | 5
